Liam: Heads up — prod P99 spike on model-serving hosts during long-context bursts. Saw tail latency jump to ~820ms from baseline ~120ms after the weekend rollout.

Liam: Logs show repeated evicter churn and reuse-miss surge:
```
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] evicter: policy=fifo evicted=128 reuse_miss=2048 reuse_hit=12
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] pager: page_fault=1 reclaim_ms=45
[2026-03-17T22:12:04Z] kv: reinsert_chain_len=7 order_flip=true
```

Priya: Which rollout? kselect or eviction change?

Liam: Experiment 33: eviction.default=fifo, batch.coalesce=8, kselect=v2 landed together.

Amanda: Noted. This smells like FIFO reinserts + longer KV lifetimes from bigger batches. If an entry gets reinserted while pager is scanning, we can get order inversion that forces extra paging.

Amanda: Profiler snapshot:
```
perf top:
  42.1%  kv_reuse_scan
  18.6%  memcpy_small_pages
  7.2%   thread-wakeup
```

Josh: Can we repro locally? Suggest loadgen cmd:
```
./loadgen --model r1 --concurrency 4 --qps 200 --context 32000 --eviction=fifo --batch_size=8 --duration 5m
```
I'll run a canary tonight.

sre-bot: deploy-bot rolled back experiment-33 on 2026-03-17T22:13:10Z :white_check_mark:

Liam: I also saw a kernel-selection diff that switches small-page memcpy into a hotpath optimized asm. Might be exposing a race w/ the pager (fast memcpy -> timing change).

Priya: Interesting — batching heuristic increased coalescing so entries live longer across request boundaries. Combined with FIFO reinserts it's plausible we get a rebalance storm.

Amanda: Actionable plan:
- repro with Josh's loadgen and upload perf + flamegraph
- add assert in pager to detect order_flip early (in debug builds)
- temporarily disable fifo for high-batch-size hosts (canary)
- add unit test for reinsertion ordering under concurrent reclaim

Liam: I'll open an issue with logs + flamegraph: https://internal.re/redwood/issue/EV-872 (flame: /s3/flame-3355554321.svg)

Priya: ack :thumbsup:

Amanda: assigning to infra and runtime for follow-up @Josh @Liam

Josh: on it, starting repro now.
